newsitem.title: TURKEY: Rebel Turk MP says new coalition seeks rule.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Turk MP says new coalition seeks rule.

text.p: A dissident Turkish government deputy said on Tuesday that his planned alternative coalition excluding the ruling Islamists would aim to rule rather than hold fresh elections.

"This government will not be for elections it will be a solution government," former trade and industry minister Yalim Erez told reporters after talks with a leftist leader on setting up a new coalition.
Erez earlier met the leader of Turkey's main opposition party, who said the two agreed fully on a coalition formula that would keep out the Islamist Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
"We are in full agreement with Erez. We will press the button this week," Motherland Party leader Mesut Yilmaz told reporters after talks with Erez, in reference to plans to topple the government.
Democratic Left Party leader Bulent Ecevit echoed Erez's view on the nature of a new government and said it may include his party and, possibly, another rival leftist group.

Erez said after meeting Yilmaz that he planned to discuss his coalition proposal as soon as possible with the deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller, leader of the conservative True Path Party (DYP) partner in the current ruling coalition.

Disagreements among the mainstream secularist parties of the left and right have thwarted previous attempts to establish a government excluding Welfare. Such divisions led to the formation of the existing coalition last June.
Erez and another former minister from the DYP resigned last month in protest at the Islamists' failure to back an army-led crackdown on religious activism.
The government has been deeply divided over the reluctance of Welfare to support reforms of the education system which it fears would erode the role of religious schools in Turkey.
It was not clear how many DYP deputies would support Erez's plan, but Yilmaz said there was support within the party -- conservative rival of his own -- for ending the coalition.
"I know there are many deputies in the DYP who share our view that this government must go immediately," Yilmaz was quoted as telling reporters by state-run Anatolian news agency.
Another dissident DYP deputy warned on Monday there could be a confidence vote to bring down the coalition if the party did not support the alternative coalition proposal.
The government has a narrow majority in parliament.
